title: RBAC v2 backfill reconciliation and SSO/SAML mapping safeguards
creator: Leah Kim
description: Objective: Safely migrate existing RBAC v1 state to RBAC v2 with a focus on reconciliation correctness, audit trail completeness, SSO/SAML group->role mapping fidelity, and admin control ergonomics. This ticket covers the design and execution of the backfill reconciliation engine, dual-write validation harness, SAML mapping checks, cutover runbook, and customer communication templates. We specifically avoid a blind cutover: this work prioritizes detection and automated remediation of mismatches and a well-tested rollback path.
background_and_rationale: RBAC v1 stored role assignments in a legacy schema (role_bindings_v1). RBAC v2 introduces scoped roles, inheritance, and fine-grained principal types (service_account, user, external_saml_group). Several customers use SAML group assertions with on-the-fly group mapping to app roles. Early migrations found edge cases (duplicate group names across IdPs, cross-tenant service accounts, stale groups). This ticket aims to enumerate those edge cases, build reconciliation tooling that produces low-risk patches, and instrument audit logs so every mapping decision is traceable and reversible.
success_criteria: Backfill job migrates 100% of active role bindings with reconciliation error rate < 0.1% on first full run
All reconciliation changes are recorded in audit logs with before/after snapshots and operator idempotency markers
Dual-write validation for new changes runs for >=14 days with zero unexpected divergence for canary customers
SAML group mapping adapter is able to detect ambiguous mappings and surface them via admin UI and migration report
Cutover runbook and rollback steps are scripted and tested in staging and one production canary org
deliverables: Reconciliation engine: diff->plan->apply pipeline with dry-run and approve modes
Dual-write shim that writes to both v1 and v2 stores with consistent hashing and conflict resolution
Audit logging enhancements to capture mapping_reason, mapping_source, operator_id, and migration_id
SAML mapping validator that flags ambiguous mappings and emits remediation actions
Admin console pages: migration report view, unresolved-mapping queue, and one-click rollback for a binding
Cutover runbook: timeline, metrics to watch, communication scripts, and rollback trigger conditions
Customer comms templates for enterprise and self-serve orgs

runbook_high_level_steps: 1) Pre-checks: run 'rbac-migrate preflight' for target orgs to collect current v1 bindings, active principals, and SAML assertion history
2) Dry-run: run reconciliation job in dry-run mode -> produce migration plan and unresolved items report
3) Resolve: surface ambiguous SAML mappings to admins; provide recommended mappings and allow accept/decline
4) Dual-write enablement: enable dual-write for target cohorts (API layer writes to v1+v2) with feature flag and monitoring
5) Backfill: execute reconciliation apply in throttled windows (configurable parallelism, default 2000 binds/hour), writing migration_id tags
6) Monitor: track reconciliation_error_rate, migration_throughput, audit_log_ingest_lags, and admin_approvals_pending
7) Canary cutover: after >=14 days of stable dual-write, flip canary orgs to read-v2-first with read-fallback to v1
8) Full cutover: schedule progressive ramp for remaining orgs; keep dual-write for 7 days post-cutover; then deprecate v1 writes after verification
9) Rollback: if divergence > threshold or severe errors, stop write to v2, revert admin UI read paths to v1, and run rollback remediations using stored migration_id
reconciliation_rules_summary: Match rules are tiered: exact principal id match > email canonicalization > SAML group external_id match > heuristic name similarity. Conflicts produce an 'ambiguous' state queued for admin review. Automatic merges only when confidence score >= 95% and mapping_source != 'external_legacy_script'
audit_logging_spec: Every migrated binding emits a structured audit event with fields: migration_id, prior_binding_snapshot (as JSON string), new_binding_snapshot (as JSON string), operator (system or user email), timestamp, confidence_score, mapping_reason, source_idp. Audit events are stored in the existing ELK pipeline and forwarded to customer-managed webhooks for enterprise orgs.
saml_mapping_notes:
- IdP variance: Google and Okta send group external IDs differently; validator normalizes both to external_id and idp_domain.
- Duplicate group names across IdPs: validator rejects ambiguous name-only mappings and recommends using external_id.
- SCIM sync gaps: flag principals with recent SCIM deltas and exclude them from auto-apply until admin confirmation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: SAML group ambiguity leading to incorrect permission grants. Mitigation: require admin approval for ambiguous cases and add a soft-deny mode where ambiguous mappings result in no-auto-apply.
Risk: Backfill performance causes throttling on metadata DB. Mitigation: implement token-bucket throttling per-tenant and a circuit-breaker threshold with alerts.
Risk: Missing audit visibility for edge-case reconciles. Mitigation: add synchronous audit-sync step that replays audit events to long-term storage before marking migration_id completed.
Risk: Dual-write divergence undetected. Mitigation: run periodic property-based tests and random sampling comparisons; escalate if divergence > 0.01% for 1h
customer_communication_templates: Enterprise email (short): We're upgrading RBAC to a more flexible, auditable model (RBAC v2). We'll run a background migration and will notify you of any ambiguous role mappings requiring your input. No immediate action required; you can opt into a staged canary. See: https://redwood.ai/docs/rbac-migration
Self-serve banner text: We're rolling out RBAC v2 for better role controls and audit logs. Expect a background migration; contact support if you see unexpected permission changes.
Support playbook snippet: For reported permission regressions, collect migration_id from audit log, run 'rbac-migrate inspect <migration_id>' and follow remediation steps in runbook section 7
testing_plan: Unit tests for reconciliation rules, integration tests for dual-write shim, end-to-end staging run with seeded orgs that include: duplicate groups, stale SCIM users, cross-tenant service accounts. Golden master verification: create a snapshot of expected v2 state from a known-good manual mapping and assert full equality after dry-run approve+apply in staging.
